title: Planting Peppers in Michigan Garden Transplanting Tight Spacing Pests Protection
reason: Describes the process of planting peppers in a garden.

tasks.task: Describe the planting process for peppers.

subtasks.text: Select the best pepper plants by checking for thick stems and healthy root systems.
Arrange and space the plants in the garden before planting.
Dig a small hole, add nutrients, and plant each pepper with the stem buried by about an inch.
Remove peppers from cups by flipping them over and crinkling the bottom.

tasks.task: Explain the benefits of tight spacing and additional plants for support and pest control.

subtasks.text: Plant peppers in a tight spacing to support each other on windy days.
Plant marigolds for pest control on the edges of the garden.
Plant cilantro and dill seeds around the border of the garden.

tasks.task: Describe the final steps to prepare the garden for the peppers.

subtasks.text: Add a layer of straw to the garden bed to retain moisture and suppress weeds.
Water the garden bed to help welcome the peppers to their new home.
